content:
Let each grid square have side length \(1\), with coordinates

\[
T=(0,0),\quad U=(1,0),\quad V=(1,2),\quad W=(2,3).
\]

The vertical segment has endpoints \((0,1)\) and \((0,3)\), while the horizontal segment has endpoints \((2,1)\) and \((4,1)\).

### 1. Rotation about \(U\)

A \(90^\circ\) clockwise rotation about \(U\) sends

\[
(0,1)\longmapsto (2,1),\qquad
(0,3)\longmapsto (4,1).
\]

Thus the vertical segment maps exactly onto the horizontal segment, so \(U\) is possible.

### 2. Rotation about \(W\)

A \(90^\circ\) counterclockwise rotation about \(W\) sends

\[
(0,1)\longmapsto (4,1),\qquad
(0,3)\longmapsto (2,1).
\]

Thus \(W\) is also possible.

A rotation taking a vertical segment to a horizontal one must be \(90^\circ\) clockwise or \(90^\circ\) counterclockwise. These two possibilities have unique centers, namely \(U\) and \(W\), so neither \(T\) nor \(V\) can be a center.

\[
\boxed{\text{C: either }U\text{ and }W}
\]
